title: [VSC-4] JetBrains: shared blocker corpus for TaskBlockerPresentation
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). First wave: no dependencies, files disjoint from the other first-wave rows. JetBrains first: this row writes the held-out corpus that VS Code's blocker row (VSC-9) must pass unchanged.

Reuse decision (VSC-0): one client-neutral JSON corpus per shared presentation, executed by both test suites (CQ-I06b pattern, moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json; rule in the header of ClientVerdictCorpusTest.kt: a disagreement is fixed or filed, never given a client-specific expectation). Each new corpus gets its own file.

Objective: block-cause logic exists three times today: JetBrains moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentation.kt (cause, badges, detail, prerequisiteIds), VS Code moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts (exported blockCause, blockedPrerequisiteIds, blockerFacts) and VS Code moe-vscode/media/board.js (its own blockCause and blockedPrerequisiteIds in browser JS). Pin the client-neutral part as a corpus, with JetBrains as the reference.

Deliverable:
- new moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-blocker.json: `{ "version": 1, "rows": [ { "id": "B01", "task": <task wire JSON>, "cause": "RESOURCE_WAIT" | "DEPENDENCY_WAIT" | "EXTERNAL_BLOCK" | null, "prerequisiteIds": [...], "needsHumanReview": true | false } ] }` (the cause names are the enum both clients already use). At least 14 rows: each cause; a non-BLOCKED status carrying stale block fields (cause null); BLOCKED with blockedOnTaskIds; a reason naming task ids, with and without blockedOnTaskIds (whatever JetBrains derives); duplicate and blank ids; resourceId together with task ids (the precedence JetBrains applies); needsHumanReview true on REVIEW and on BLOCKED, independent of cause; missing optional fields.
- new moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/BlockerCorpusTest.kt: parses each task with MoeJson.parseTask, asserts TaskBlockerPresentation.cause(task)?.name, prerequisiteIds(task) (order included) and the badges' needs-human-review flag against the row, asserts unique `B[0-9]{2}` ids, and reports every failing id at once.
If a row exposes a JetBrains bug, fix TaskBlockerPresentation.kt here and name it in the summary; never bend a row to a bug.

Not in scope: VS Code files (VSC-9), TaskBlockerPresentationTest.kt (unchanged), wording and bundle text (the clients word blocker facts differently on purpose; only the fields above are shared).

Verification (WSL has no JDK): take the `jetbrains-gradle` lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease); `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /mnt/d/moe-scratch/<dir>`; overlay this task's files; run `cmd.exe /d /c 'set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\moe-scratch\<dir>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun'` (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-snapshot-gradle-test); release the lease even on failure.
definitionOfDone: moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-blocker.json exists with version 1 and at least 14 rows with unique B[0-9]{2} ids, covering every case listed in the description.

BlockerCorpusTest.kt parses each row's task with MoeJson.parseTask and asserts the cause name, prerequisiteIds (order included) and the needs-human-review flag against the row, reporting all failing ids at once.
A scratch-copy mutant that makes TaskBlockerPresentation.cause return a cause for a non-BLOCKED task makes BlockerCorpusTest fail (mutant discarded afterwards).
The full JetBrains suite passes in a git-archive snapshot under the jetbrains-gradle lease: `gradlew.bat test --rerun` reports BUILD SUCCESSFUL, with the JUnit total in the summary.
The diff touches only the two new files, plus TaskBlockerPresentation.kt if a row exposed a JetBrains bug (named in the summary).

implementationPlan.description:
Write the held-out corpus moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-blocker.json with the Write tool (global rail: tracked files only through Edit/Write).
Shape: `{ "version": 1, "rows": [ { "id", "note", "task", "cause", "prerequisiteIds", "needsHumanReview" } ] }`, 2-space pretty-printed like client-delivery.json, LF, trailing newline.
- `id` is B01..B17; `note` is one line naming the case.
- `task` is a daemon task wire object. It always holds "id": "task-bNN" (the row id lowercased) and "epicId": "epic-corpus", because MoeJson.parseState drops a task without epicId. Its other members come only from status, needsHumanReview, blockedReason, blockedOnTaskIds, blockedResourceId, blockedFromStatus and blockedAt.
- `cause` is "RESOURCE_WAIT", "DEPENDENCY_WAIT", "EXTERNAL_BLOCK" or JSON null. `prerequisiteIds` is an array of strings. `needsHumanReview` is a JSON boolean.
Every expectation below was computed from TaskBlockerPresentation.kt at HEAD and cross-checked by a simulation: write them literally. Note the facts it encodes:
- prerequisiteIds(task) is the raw recorded list. It ignores status (only cause is status-gated), keeps order and duplicates, keeps each id verbatim (never trimmed) and drops blank ids.
- Nothing is ever parsed out of blockedReason.
Ids: A = task-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef, B = task-fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210, C = task-1111aaaa2222bbbb3333cccc4444dddd. Notation: `task members -> cause, prerequisiteIds, needsHumanReview` (id/epicId omitted below).
B01 status BLOCKED, blockedResourceId "jetbrains-gradle", blockedFromStatus "WORKING", blockedReason "Waiting on the gradle lease.", blockedAt "2026-11-02T10:00:00.000Z" -> RESOURCE_WAIT, [], false.
B02 BLOCKED, blockedOnTaskIds [A, B], blockedFromStatus "PLANNING", blockedReason "Waiting on two prerequisites." -> DEPENDENCY_WAIT, [A, B], false.
B03 BLOCKED, blockedFromStatus "REVIEW", blockedReason "A human has to decide." -> EXTERNAL_BLOCK, [], false.
B04 status WORKING with stale blockedResourceId "jetbrains-gradle", blockedOnTaskIds [A], blockedReason "Old block.", blockedFromStatus "WORKING" -> null, [A], false.
B05 status BACKLOG, no blocker fields -> null, [], false.
B06 status REVIEW, needsHumanReview true -> null, [], true.
B07 BLOCKED, blockedReason "Needs a decision.", needsHumanReview true -> EXTERNAL_BLOCK, [], true.
B08 BLOCKED, blockedReason "Waiting on " + A + " to land.", no blockedOnTaskIds -> EXTERNAL_BLOCK, [], false (the reason is never parsed).
B09 BLOCKED, blockedOnTaskIds [C], blockedReason "Waiting on " + A + " as well." -> DEPENDENCY_WAIT, [C], false.
B10 BLOCKED, blockedOnTaskIds [A, "", B, "   ", A, "\t", " " + C + " "] -> DEPENDENCY_WAIT, [A, B, A, " " + C + " "], false (duplicates kept, blanks dropped, padding kept).
B11 BLOCKED, blockedOnTaskIds ["", " ", "\n"] -> EXTERNAL_BLOCK, [], false (only blanks fall through).
B12 BLOCKED, blockedResourceId "bench-box-1", blockedOnTaskIds [A] -> RESOURCE_WAIT, [A], false (the resource wins; the ids are still reported).
B13 BLOCKED, blockedResourceId "   ", blockedOnTaskIds [A] -> DEPENDENCY_WAIT, [A], false (a blank resource falls through).
B14 BLOCKED and nothing else -> EXTERNAL_BLOCK, [], false (every optional field missing; needsHumanReview absent reads false).
B15 BLOCKED with blockedResourceId, blockedOnTaskIds, blockedReason, blockedFromStatus and blockedAt all JSON null -> EXTERNAL_BLOCK, [], false.
B16 BLOCKED, blockedOnTaskIds [] -> EXTERNAL_BLOCK, [], false.
B17 status REVIEW with stale blockedOnTaskIds [A], blockedReason "Old block.", blockedFromStatus "WORKING" and needsHumanReview true -> null, [A], true.
DoD coverage map:
- each cause: B01, B02, B03;
- a non-BLOCKED status with stale fields: B04, B17;
- BLOCKED with blockedOnTaskIds: B02;
- a reason naming task ids, without and with blockedOnTaskIds: B08, B09;
- duplicate and blank ids: B10, B11;
- a resource id together with task ids: B12 (blank resource: B13);
- needsHumanReview true on REVIEW and on BLOCKED, independent of cause: B06, B17, B07;
- missing optional fields: B14, B15, B16.
Leave out wrong-kind values (numbers or booleans where strings belong): MoeJsonTest already pins that strictness. Leave out Unicode-only blank ids too: Kotlin isBlank and JS trim disagree on U+FEFF and U+001C..U+001F, an exotic edge the daemon never serves, recorded in planningNotes.
implementationPlan.note: Wrote corpus B01..B17 per plan; JSON parses (17 rows). Dirty paths of peers left untouched.
Wrote BlockerCorpusTest.kt with two tests; gate next.

implementationPlan.description:
Gate and mutation proof in a snapshot under the jetbrains-gradle lease, never in the shared tree (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease, mem:gotcha-jetbrains-snapshot-gradle-test, mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl: WSL has no JDK; from bash, single-quote the whole cmd string and pass --tests unquoted).
- Take the lease with moe.acquire_resource {resourceId:"jetbrains-gradle", taskId, workerId, note}. If it is busy, park with moe.report_blocked {resourceId:"jetbrains-gradle"} (seat kept).
- Hold the lease only around the gradle runs, and release it with moe.release_resource even on failure.
- Run every command from the repo root /mnt/d/projexts/moes.
1) Focused run: build the snapshot exactly as the checkRef does (its part before `&& cmd.exe`), then run `cmd.exe /d /c 'set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\moe-scratch\vsc4-gate\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.toolwindow.BlockerCorpusTest --rerun'`. It passes with 2 tests (check TEST-com.moe.toolwindow.BlockerCorpusTest.xml).
2) Mutant, in the SNAPSHOT copy only (scratch outside the checkout, so a shell edit is allowed there): `sed -i '/if (task.status != BLOCKED_STATUS) return null/d' /mnt/d/moe-scratch/vsc4-gate/moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentation.kt`. Confirm with diff that exactly one line went: the architect dry-ran it, and the file is UTF-8 with LF endings. Re-run the focused command. It must FAIL, naming B04, B05, B06 and B17 (the non-BLOCKED rows now get a cause) and no other planned row. Record the ids for the summary.
3) Run the checkRef verbatim. It rebuilds a clean snapshot, which discards the mutant, and runs the full suite. Confirm BUILD SUCCESSFUL and that :test executed. Then `cmp` the three copied files against the shared tree, and sum tests, failures, errors and skipped over the snapshot's build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml for the JUnit total.
Error handling for a red run:
- A red row before the mutant is most likely a corpus typo: re-derive it from TaskBlockerPresentation.kt first.
- Change TaskBlockerPresentation.kt only for a genuine JetBrains bug. Name the fix in the summary and list the file in complete_step.modifiedFiles; the checkRef already copies it.
- "Could not receive a message from the daemon" is a gradlew client OOM (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-client-oom): rerun, never count it as a result.
- A failure in an untouched file that ties to a peer's wip checkpoint follows mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint.
- Never stop Gradle daemons or kill processes by name.
implementationPlan.note: Focused: 2 tests pass. Mutant (status gate removed, snapshot only) fails exactly B04,B05,B06,B17. Full suite in clean snapshot: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 551 tests, 0 failures/errors/skipped. Lease released. No JetBrains bug found.

Self-review: B12 (precedence), B13 (blank resource), B10 (no trim/dedupe), B11 (blanks), B08 (reason not parsed), B06/B17 (attention independent), B04/B05/B06/B17 (status gate, mutant-proven) each pin a named mutation. Every DoD case maps to a row. Corpus is plain JSON. git status -- moe-jetbrains shows only the two new files.

BlockerCorpusTest replays it through both MoeJson task paths. VS Code's VSC-9 (task-06dda5c1) replays the same bytes through TaskDetailPanel.ts and media/board.js. sourceAssumptions: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentation.kt: cause() returns null unless status is BLOCKED, then RESOURCE_WAIT for a non-blank blockedResourceId, DEPENDENCY_WAIT for non-empty prerequisiteIds, else EXTERNAL_BLOCK; prerequisiteIds() = blockedOnTaskIds.orEmpty().filter { it.isNotBlank() } with no status gate; badges().needsHumanReview = task.needsHumanReview.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rows pin only the client-neutral outputs (cause name, raw prerequisiteIds, attention flag), never wording. The test parses through both parseTask (the DoD's path) and parseState, because the two build blocker fields separately. Blank, duplicate and padded ids are not daemon-servable today (report_blocked dedupes and drops unknown ids), but the slice description asks for them as legacy-data rows, and all three implementations already agree on them. Rejected: wrong-kind rows (MoeJsonTest covers parser strictness). Rejected: Unicode-only blank ids. Kotlin isBlank treats U+001C..U+001F as blank, and JS trim treats U+FEFF as blank, so pinning either would force VS Code to port Java's whitespace table. It is a known exotic divergence; leave it unpinned.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: VS Code already mirrors the rule twice: TaskDetailPanel.ts exports blockCause/blockedPrerequisiteIds, and media/board.js has its own copy. Both have the same guards (non-blank strings, arrays only, order and duplicates kept, no status gate on the id list), so VSC-9 should pass unchanged. The status gate and resource-over-dependency precedence are documented in the KDoc of TaskBlockerPresentation.cause.
planningNotes.risks: A corpus typo is the likeliest red row: re-derive it before touching TaskBlockerPresentation.kt. Escape tabs and newlines in JSON strings (\t, \n). B10's padded id keeps its spaces. Apply the mutant only to the snapshot copy. git archive HEAD carries peers' wip checkpoints (mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint).
